title: US Air Force Moves to Nearly Triple F-15EX Fleet to 268 Jets as Rheinmetall Eyes €12.4B German Boxer Program
subhead: The Pentagon's fiscal 2027 budget request would turn the F-15EX from a modest replacement into a 268-aircraft, $36.9 billion production run for Boeing, while Rheinmetall expects a €12.4 billion initial award under Germany's Arminius armored-vehicle plan. Both signal a shift from buying new platforms to scaling up proven, in-production systems.

sections.heading: US Air Force Plans to Nearly Triple F-15EX Fleet to 268 Aircraft
sections.body:
The U.S. Air Force is seeking to nearly triple its planned F-15EX Eagle II fleet from 98 to 268 aircraft under the fiscal 2027 President's Budget, according to a U.S. Department of War report cited by Defence Industry Europe. The expansion adds 170 jets, extends procurement through fiscal 2031 and raises estimated acquisition costs to $36.93 billion.

The revised plan covers 266 production fighters and two development aircraft, up from a June 2024 baseline of 96 production jets. Procurement accounts for almost $35 billion of the estimate, with an average unit cost projected at $131.6 million in then-year dollars. The Air Force would buy 24 jets in fiscal 2027, 24 in 2028, 28 in 2029 and 36 in each of 2030 and 2031.

The expansion turns what was a smaller replacement program into a long-term production run for Boeing, which must raise output to two aircraft a month to meet delivery requirements. As of April 2026, Boeing had delivered 18 F-15EXs against a contractual requirement for 33, after a 15-week strike at its St. Louis facility in 2025 halted production. The delays are expected to push the program past its July 2027 full-operational-capability threshold, prompting a formal schedule rebaseline.
sections.whyItMatters: The Air Force is betting on a mature, in-production airframe to replace aging F-15C/Ds rather than waiting on next-generation programs, but the plan rests on Boeing's ability to recover from production and supply-chain setbacks.

sections.heading: Rheinmetall Expects €12.4 Billion Initial Award Under Germany's Arminius Boxer Program
sections.body:
Rheinmetall expects to secure about €12.4 billion of vehicle business from Germany's Arminius procurement program by the end of 2026, Chief Executive Armin Papperger said on the company's second-quarter earnings call, per Defence Industry Europe. Because Rheinmetall and KNDS Deutschland each hold 50% of the Artec consortium, the full value of the initial vehicle package could approach €25 billion.

Final negotiations between Artec and the Bundeswehr were expected in the second week of September, with Bundestag funding consideration scheduled for 9 December. Papperger said a separate support agreement of about €4 billion would bring Rheinmetall's expected business from the initial package to roughly €14.4 billion. Two further options could push the program's theoretical ceiling toward €77 billion, though those orders are neither agreed nor funded.

German media reports indicate the initial order could cover about 1,800 GTK Boxer vehicles, with options adding up to 5,500 Boxers by around 2040 — on top of 861 already ordered. Variants under consideration include the Schakal infantry fighting vehicle, the RCH 155 self-propelled howitzer and air-defense versions with the Skyranger 30 turret.
sections.whyItMatters: Arminius would be one of the largest additions to Rheinmetall's order book — already at €80.4 billion backlog — and locks in European armored-vehicle production work well into the next decade as NATO members raise spending.

sections.heading: F-35 Weapons Roadmap: AARGM-ER, LRASM and JSM in 2027, Meteor and SPEAR 3 in 2032
sections.body:
The U.S. F-35 program plans to field a broad package of new weapons in September 2027, according to the F-35 Modernized Selected Acquisition Report prepared for the fiscal 2027 budget and detailed by Defence Industry Europe. The package includes AARGM-ER (anti-radiation), LRASM (anti-ship), the Joint Strike Missile and the GBU-53/B StormBreaker glide bomb, expanding the stealth fighter's role in air-defense suppression, maritime strike and attacks on moving targets.

A second weapons wave is planned for September 2032, including the Meteor beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile, the UK-specific SPEAR 3 stand-off weapon and a low-observable pylon for LRASM, JASSM and JASSM-ER. The roadmap also includes the 'Six in the Bay' configuration in September 2030, raising the internal missile load from four to six.

The weapons plan is tied to the Technology Refresh 3 computing upgrade, which the report says is being installed in production aircraft but whose complex software development continues to present difficulties. Nine new flight-science aircraft are planned to replace the aging F-35 test fleet.
sections.whyItMatters: The roadmap reflects the F-35 program's shift from building fleet numbers toward expanding the combat value of aircraft already in service, but delivery depends on TR-3 software maturity — a persistent schedule risk.

sections.heading: US Plans Up to $2 Billion Underground Network for Sentinel ICBM at Malmstrom
sections.body:
The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers updated solicitation W9128F26SM024 on September 4 for a military construction project worth between $1.4 billion and $2 billion to build up to 3,581 km (2,225 miles) of underground communications infrastructure for the LGM-35A Sentinel ICBM at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, per Army Recognition. Industry responses are due September 24.

The project would connect Sentinel launch facilities, launch centers and command infrastructure across the Malmstrom missile field, which currently operates 150 Minuteman III launch facilities. The Northrop Grumman-led Sentinel program plans 400 operational missiles while recapitalizing 450 silos and more than 600 facilities across roughly 103,600 km².

The Pentagon's 2024 Nunn-McCurdy review placed the restructured Sentinel program at approximately $140.9 billion, with command-and-launch infrastructure contributing heavily to the increase. The Malmstrom requirement follows the first in-field Sentinel utility-corridor work near Kimball, Nebraska, in June 2026, which involved more than 37 km of fiber-optic infrastructure.
sections.whyItMatters: The scale of the underground network shows that replacing Minuteman III is as much an infrastructure program as a missile program — and that ground construction, not missile development, may set the pace of US land-based nuclear modernization.

sections.heading: UK to Pair F-35B Fighters With Jet-Powered Drones Under Project VANQUISH
sections.body:
Britain will test jet-powered drones alongside F-35B fighters under Project VANQUISH as the Royal Navy builds a mixed crewed and autonomous carrier force, according to the UK Ministry of Defence's 2026 Defence Investment Plan, per Defence Industry Europe. The trials form part of Project PANTHEON, a nearly £240 million investment in systems for a future Hybrid Carrier Air Wing.

The ministry has not identified the drone model, number of aircraft, suppliers or schedule for the VANQUISH trials. The plan sits within a wider commitment of more than £5 billion for autonomous military systems through 2030, which the ministry describes as its largest-ever drone investment. A separate £300 million Collaborative Combat Aircraft program aims to fly a concept demonstrator by 2030.

The Defence Investment Plan assigns £2.2 billion to the F-35 fleet and £510 million to the Queen Elizabeth-class carriers over the next four years, and records the first air-to-air engagement of a drone by a British F-35B over Jordan.
sections.whyItMatters: The UK is committing to a carrier air wing that pairs crewed F-35Bs with autonomous jets and drones, a model that could reshape how European navies think about carrier aviation mass and cost.

sections.heading: BAE Systems Ties Golden Dome Role to $1.2 Billion Epoch 2 Missile-Warning Program
sections.body:
BAE Systems expects its U.S. space business to play a significant role in the Golden Dome missile-defense architecture, including through the $1.2 billion Epoch 2 resilient missile-warning and tracking program, President and CEO of BAE Systems Inc. Tom Arseneault said on the company's first-half 2026 earnings call, per Defence Industry Europe. BAE completed a preliminary design review for Epoch 2 earlier in 2026, which will provide a multi-satellite constellation and ground command-and-control for Golden Dome.

Sales in BAE's Space & Mission Systems business rose almost 30% in the first half of 2026 year-on-year. CFO Brad Greve said the unit generated £1.6 billion of orders in the first half, with Electronic Systems sales up 11% led by 29% growth in space. BAE cited the Raytheon UTC spinoffs and Ball Aerospace among acquisitions that added durable revenue growth.
sections.whyItMatters: Golden Dome is becoming a concrete revenue driver for defense primes, and BAE's space growth shows how homeland missile-defense priorities are reshaping the US defense industrial base.

sections.heading: EDGE Completes AKAER Acquisition; HII Wins $336M Ford-Class Carrier Contract
sections.body:
EDGE Group has completed its acquisition of Brazilian aerospace engineering specialist AKAER after all closing conditions were met, per Defence Industry Europe. SIATT will hold a minority stake in AKAER to preserve its status as a Strategic Defence Company in Brazil. AKAER, founded in 1992 and based in São José dos Campos, has accumulated more than 10 million engineering hours across military and commercial aerospace programs, and the two companies already collaborate on unmanned systems development.

Separately, Huntington Ingalls Industries secured a $336 million contract to begin advance material procurement for the future USS William J. Clinton (CVN 82), the fifth Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carrier, with work scheduled through March 2039 at Newport News Shipbuilding. HII is also completing delivery trials for the USS John F. Kennedy and progressing on the USS Enterprise (CVN 80) and the fourth carrier, Doris Miller.
sections.whyItMatters: EDGE's AKAER deal extends Gulf defense investment into Latin American aerospace and unmanned systems, while the HII award keeps the US carrier industrial base funded through the late 2030s.

bottomLine: Today's defense industry news is dominated by scale-up decisions on proven platforms: the US Air Force's move to nearly triple the F-15EX fleet, Rheinmetall's expected €12.4 billion Arminius award, and the F-35's weapons expansion roadmap all point to a procurement environment favoring in-production systems over new-start programs. The Sentinel ICBM's $2 billion underground network underscores that nuclear modernization is increasingly an infrastructure challenge, while the UK's Project VANQUISH and BAE's Golden Dome role show autonomous systems and missile defense driving the next wave of spending. Across the board, the theme is industrial capacity — can primes deliver at the volumes governments are now ordering.
sources: Defence Industry Europe, Army Recognition, Financial Express, Reuters, Breaking Defense, The Guardian, Kyiv Independent, Defense News
